# Overview

Cloak and Celerity is a three-mechanic Esper deck in which one engine feeds the other two. Eerie is the engine: whenever an enchantment you control enters, every Eerie creature triggers. Balemurk Leech turns each of those triggers into life loss for each opponent, and life loss for an opponent is exactly the condition that raises your speed. So the Eerie engine is the fuel line for Start your engines, and the Max speed payoffs come online in the mid game without any additional work.

The enchantments doing the triggering are deliberately cheap and repeatable: Lightwheel Enhancements costs a single white mana, carries Start your engines, and at max speed can be cast again from the graveyard, which makes it a recurring Eerie trigger. Nowhere to Run is a flash removal spell that happens to be an enchantment, so it triggers the whole team while killing something. Momentum Breaker is an edict that also starts the engines. Six enchantments plus four Balemurk Leeches means a hand of two enchantments and one Leech drains for four or five points over the first few turns while the board develops.

Disguise supplies the resilient half of the board. Unyielding Gatekeeper and Nightdrinker Moroii can be cast face down for three generic mana — colourless, which is a real benefit in a three-colour deck built on basics — as 2/2 creatures with ward 2. Ward 2 makes them awkward to remove, and turning them face up later is where the value sits: the Gatekeeper exiles a nonland permanent, the Moroii becomes a 4/2 flier. Both flips happen on your schedule, which is what a deck like this wants.

The finish is The Speed Demon. It is a 5/5 flying trampler whose end-step trigger draws cards equal to your speed, so by the time your speed is 4 it is drawing four cards every turn and attacking over the top. Rogue's Passage makes it unblockable for four mana, and Avishkar Raceway keeps your speed ticking from the land drop itself. Swiftwing Assailant gains vigilance at max speed, so it attacks and still blocks, and Amonkhet Raceway gives a surprise hasty Demon or Moroii out of nowhere.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | What happens |
|-------|--------------|
| Turns 1-2 | Optimistic Scavenger or Lightwheel Enhancements converts the first white mana into an Eerie body and an Eerie trigger; Balemurk Leech is the priority two-drop because it starts the drain and the speed clock |
| Turns 2-4 | Unyielding Gatekeeper and Nightdrinker Moroii come down face down as 2/2s with ward 2 for three generic mana, while Nowhere to Run or Get Lost answers the first real threat and still triggers Eerie |
| Turns 3-5 | Entity Tracker (flash) refills the hand on every enchantment, Gremlin Tamer builds a Gremlin swarm, Victor, Valgavoth's Seneschal turns the third Eerie trigger of a turn into a reanimation |
| Turns 5-7 | The Speed Demon lands as a 5/5 flier, draws your speed in cards every end step, and closes with Rogue's Passage or the Moroii and Gremlin tokens |

## Lands as engines

| Land | Role |
|------|------|
| Avishkar Raceway | Win-condition land and the cheapest speed enabler in the deck: the land itself has Start your engines!, so it sets your speed to 1 on turn one with no spell, and at max speed it loots every turn while the Demon's draw trigger gets bigger |
| Rogue's Passage | Win-condition land: four mana and a tap makes The Speed Demon, Nightdrinker Moroii or a counter-loaded Optimistic Scavenger unblockable, which converts a stalled board into lethal |
| Amonkhet Raceway | Win-condition support: at max speed it grants haste, which is how a top-decked Speed Demon or Moroii attacks the turn it lands |
| Fountainport | Turns Gremlin Tamer tokens into cards, and its Fish and Treasure modes give the deck something to do with five spare mana at instant speed |
| Plains / Swamp / Island | The entire coloured base. There are no dual lands in the deck, so the colour demands are kept low on purpose: 6 white sources, 7 black and 5 blue, with every three-colour card (Victor, Gremlin Tamer) deliberately cheap |

## Curve and mana

The 36 non-land cards are 4 one-drops, 20 two-drops, 5 three-drops, 5 four-drops and 2 five-drops, for an average converted mana cost of 2.47. The deck is built to double-spell from turn three: the two-mana slot holds Balemurk Leech, Optimistic Scavenger support, Lightwheel Enhancements, Nowhere to Run, Get Lost and Bitter Triumph, and the three-mana slot holds Entity Tracker and Victor. The top of the curve is The Speed Demon and the two four-mana fliers, and nothing above five.

Twenty-four lands, of which six produce only colourless mana (two Avishkar Raceway, two Rogue's Passage, one Amonkhet Raceway, one Fountainport). That is the cost of the land engine, and it is affordable because Disguise lets Unyielding Gatekeeper and Nightdrinker Moroii be deployed for three generic mana. A seven-card hand with two coloured sources and a Leech is a keep; a hand that leans on white and blue for a Gremlin Tamer on curve is not.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Turn one is Optimistic Scavenger or Lightwheel Enhancements. Both are one mana, both are Eerie triggers later, and the Scavenger turns every later enchantment into a +1/+1 counter. Balemurk Leech is the two-drop you want most: it does not need to attack or block to do its job, and every enchantment you cast after it starts draining.

Do not rush the face-down creatures onto the board. Unyielding Gatekeeper and Nightdrinker Moroii are best played face down when you have three spare mana and nothing better to do, because a 2/2 with ward 2 blocks almost nothing profitably in the first turns and eats a removal spell awkwardly. Their value is the flip later, and ward 2 means they usually survive to flip.

## Mid game

From turn three, count enchantments. Nowhere to Run, Momentum Breaker, Lightwheel Enhancements and the Room-unlock clause on Eerie mean every enchantment you cast is worth one trigger per Eerie creature. With a Leech and a Scavenger out, a single Nowhere to Run is a kill spell, a -3/-3 shrink and two counters on your board. Entity Tracker with flash lets you hold up three mana and still develop, so an opposing attack step is a fine time to add another Eerie trigger.

Victor, Valgavoth's Seneschal is the engine's high end. Three separate Eerie resolutions in one turn give you surveil 2, then an opponent discards a card, then you put a creature card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control. Two cheap enchantments plus Victor is often enough to hit the reanimation mode, and the discard mode is a real answer to a control deck's sweeper.

## The combo turn

1. Have speed at 4 (Avishkar Raceway on turn one plus three separate turns where an opponent lost life — Balemurk Leech's drain does this without attacking) and The Speed Demon in hand.
2. Cast The Speed Demon. It is a 5/5 with flying and trample, so it usually attacks over the top immediately if you have hit max speed that turn, or it closes the following turn.
3. At the beginning of your end step, draw cards equal to your speed — four — and lose four life. The life loss is real; you should be at 15 or more when you start this, which is normal because the deck's own drain is one-directional.
4. Convert the extra cards into more drain: every extra Balemurk Leech doubles the per-enchantment damage, and every extra enchantment is another round of triggers.
5. Rogue's Passage plus four spare mana makes the Demon unblockable on the attack, which is the turn the game usually ends.

## Win condition 2

The drain and swarm plan does not need the Demon at all. Four Balemurk Leeches mean each enchantment is four points of life loss. Gremlin Tamer makes a 1/1 Gremlin per Eerie trigger, Optimistic Scavenger puts counters on the best body, and Fountainport turns spare Gremlins into cards. In a long game the drain alone kills: a turn with two enchantments and two Leeches is four points with no combat, and Victor's discard mode and the removal suite keep the opponent off their own plan while it happens.

The third route is the air force: Nightdrinker Moroii, Swiftwing Assailant and the Demon are all fliers, and Rogue's Passage or Amonkhet Raceway's haste pushes the biggest one through for the last points. Because the deck's speed also comes from a land and never from a creature, it keeps ticking even in the turns where the board is stuck.

## Mulligan guide

Keep two to four lands plus at least one of Balemurk Leech, Optimistic Scavenger or an enchantment. The deck has twenty two-drops, so a three-land hand with two spells is excellent and five lands is a flood — ship it. Ship one-land hands, hands with no black source (Balemurk Leech is the engine and seven lands make black), and hands that need both a Plains and an Island for the same turn. A keep with a Leech and any cheap enchantment is a keep: that pair is the whole engine, and the deck's removal is cheap enough to buy the turns the drain needs.

## Key interactions and edge cases

- Eerie triggers only on enchantments you control. The deck's enchantments are Lightwheel Enhancements, Nowhere to Run and Momentum Breaker — the Disguise creatures are creatures, not enchantments, and turning one face up is not an enchantment entering.
- Speed does not go up on its own: it increases once on each of your turns when an opponent loses life. Balemurk Leech's drain is the most reliable trigger because it does not need a successful attack, and life loss from the drain counts even if it happens during your end step.
- A face-down Disguise creature is a 2/2 with no name, no types and ward 2. Unyielding Gatekeeper is an Elephant Cleric once flipped, not a Detective, and the flip is a special action you can take at any time you could cast an instant.
- Unyielding Gatekeeper's turn-up exiles another target nonland permanent. Exiling your own permanent returns it tapped, which is a clean way to reset Optimistic Scavenger or reuse an enters-the-battlefield ability; exiling an opponent's gives them a 2/2 Detective token, so pick the target that gains you the most.
- Nightdrinker Moroii costs 3 life when it enters face up. Flip it when you are not in a race, or when the 4/2 flying body is worth more than the life.
- Nowhere to Run switches off hexproof and ward for your removal for as long as it stays on the battlefield, and its own -3/-3 effect is a permanent shrink, not a damage effect, so it also answers indestructible creatures by killing the ones with 3 or less toughness.
- Lightwheel Enhancements at max speed can be cast from the graveyard, but it is an Aura: you need a creature or Vehicle to enchant, so keep one alive before you spend the mana.
- Get Lost gives the opponent two Map tokens; use it on the threat you cannot otherwise answer, and prefer Bitter Triumph when you have a card to spare, since Bitter Triumph has no downside for them.
- Bitter Triumph's additional cost is a discard or 3 life. Discard a second copy of a legendary card, an extra land or a Lightwheel Enhancements you plan to cast from the graveyard later.
- Fountainport needs a token to draw; Gremlin Tamer supplies them, and its Fish mode is the plan when you are flooded but have no tokens.
- The manabase has no dual lands, so count coloured sources: 6 white, 7 black, 5 blue, and six lands that produce only colourless mana. Sequence the colourless lands after your coloured ones unless you are actually casting a face-down creature.
- The Speed Demon's draw trigger costs life equal to your speed. At speed 4 that is four life every turn, so do not flip the Demon on at 6 life and expect to survive your own end step.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|----------|------|
| Aggro | Momentum Breaker's edict, Nowhere to Run's -3/-3 and Get Lost or Bitter Triumph answer the first threats, while Balemurk Leech drains from turn two and the Eerie tokens block. The deck usually wins the race because its damage does not need a successful attack |
| Midrange | The deck has more value engines than raw stats: Entity Tracker draws on every enchantment, Victor reanimates, and the Demon draws four a turn. Trade with the Gremlins, not the fliers, and keep the drain running |
| Control | Disguise creatures are hard to sweep profitably because the flip is optional, Lightwheel Enhancements can be rebought from the graveyard at max speed, and Fountainport converts dead tokens into cards. Victor's second Eerie mode strips a card from their hand before a wrath |
| Combo | The drain is a clock with no attack step, and the removal suite plus Victor's discard mode disrupts a setup turn. Hold Bitter Triumph for the lynchpin creature rather than spending it early |

Added 3 Lightwheel Enhancements (one mana, Eerie trigger, start your engines, rebuyable at max speed) and 1 extra Nowhere to Run | T4 0.621 to 0.638, P(4 lands) 0.615 to 0.647, synergy 73.4 to 73.9 |

Flag: the sim gate (52) was not cleared in any round — the final list sampled 48.7 to 51.6 across eight 100-game runs while synergy, curve and land-drop gates all passed comfortably. The simulation is a mirror match, so it sits at about 50 percent by construction and the difference between the rounds is inside its noise band.
